You are implementing part of a Node.js (ESM, zero-dependency) port of a Python script.

FIRST: read /workspace/CONTRACT.md in full. It is the authoritative spec.
ALSO read /output/lib/pyvalues.mjs — the shared value model, already written. Do NOT modify it
(if you find an actual bug in it, report it in your final message instead of editing).

HARD RULES (violating any of these invalidates the whole deliverable):
- ESM only: 'import'/'export'. Never 'require', never 'module.exports'.
- All files end in .mjs and every relative import includes the .mjs suffix.
- Zero npm packages. Only node: builtins, and only if genuinely needed.
- The identifier JSON must never appear in your code. No JSON.parse/JSON.stringify.
- RegExp is forbidden: no /regex/ literals, no new RegExp, and no String method call that
  takes a regex (.match/.matchAll/.search/.test, or .replace/.split with a regex).
  String .split/.replace/.startsWith/.endsWith/.indexOf/.slice/.charCodeAt with plain
  STRING arguments are fine. All pattern matching must be hand-written character loops.
- Do not shell out to python and do not embed Python.

You can observe the reference behaviour any time with:
  /workspace/dataset/test2_executable --a "<python expression>"
Never run the 'python' command. Use the binary.

Write clean, well-organised code with brief comments explaining the PyYAML/CPython
behaviour being mirrored. Only create the files assigned to you.

YOUR ASSIGNMENT: write /output/lib/yaml/nodes.mjs, events.mjs, resolver.mjs, representer.mjs, serializer.mjs, dumper.mjs

MODULE — the PyYAML front half. You write SIX files under /output/lib/yaml/.
Another agent writes /output/lib/yaml/emitter.mjs; code against the interface below.

/output/lib/yaml/nodes.mjs
  export class Node { constructor(tag, value, style=null) }
  export class ScalarNode extends Node   // .style is null | '' | "'" | '"' | '|' | '>'
  export class SequenceNode extends Node // .value is an array of Nodes; .flowStyle
  export class MappingNode extends Node  // .value is an array of [keyNode, valueNode]; .flowStyle
  export const TAG = { str:'tag:yaml.org,2002:str', int:…, float:…, bool:…, null:…,
                       seq:…, map:…, set:…, binary:…, pythonTuple:'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/tuple',
                       pythonComplex:'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/complex', … }

/output/lib/yaml/events.mjs
  Plain classes mirroring PyYAML's events, with exactly these fields:
    StreamStartEvent{encoding}  StreamEndEvent{}
    DocumentStartEvent{explicit, version, tags}  DocumentEndEvent{explicit}
    AliasEvent{anchor}
    ScalarEvent{anchor, tag, implicit, value, style}     // implicit is [bool, bool]
    SequenceStartEvent{anchor, tag, implicit, flowStyle}  SequenceEndEvent{}
    MappingStartEvent{anchor, tag, implicit, flowStyle}   MappingEndEvent{}
  Give each class a static/instance discriminant the emitter can switch on, e.g.
  a readonly 'kind' string field ('StreamStart', 'ScalarEvent', …) AND keep the classes
  exported so instanceof works. Also export helper predicates
  isNodeEvent(e) / isCollectionStartEvent(e) / isScalarEvent(e).

/output/lib/yaml/resolver.mjs
  export function resolveScalar(value)          // -> tag string
  export function resolveSequence()             // -> TAG.seq
  export function resolveMapping()              // -> TAG.map
  Implement PyYAML's implicit resolvers, keyed by first character, tried in
  REGISTRATION ORDER (bool, float, int, merge, null, timestamp, value, yaml).
  The exact patterns are listed in /workspace/CONTRACT.md — transcribe them into
  hand-written character scanners. NO RegExp. Watch these confirmed cases:
    'true'/'yes'/'on'/'off' -> bool;  '1e5' -> str (float needs a '.' and a SIGNED exponent);
    '0o17' -> str;  '012' -> int (octal);  '0x1F' -> int;  '1_000' -> int;
    '1:2' and '12:00' -> int (sexagesimal) but '1:60' -> str;
    '.inf'/'.nan' -> float;  'nan' -> str;  '' -> null;  '=' -> value;  '<<' -> merge;
    '2024-01-15' and '2024-01-15T14:30:00Z' -> timestamp;  '~' -> null;  'y'/'n' -> str.
  Verify every one of those with the binary (a str whose text resolves to a non-str tag
  gets quoted in the output, which is directly observable).

/output/lib/yaml/representer.mjs
  export class Representer { constructor(); represent(data) -> Node }
  A fresh instance per dump. Mirror PyYAML's Representer (the UNSAFE one) exactly:
  representedObjects keyed by objectId(data) from ../pyvalues.mjs, ignoreAliases(data)
  true for PY_NONE, empty PyTuple, and any str/bytes/bool/int/float.
  Dispatch on exact type: PyNone->null 'null'; string->str; PyBytes->binary
  (base64Encodebytes from ../pyrepr.mjs, style '|'); PyBool->bool 'true'/'false';
  BigInt->int; Number->float (see CONTRACT for represent_float, including the
  ".0e" fixup and repr(...).toLowerCase()); PyList->seq; PyTuple->python/tuple;
  PyDict->map; PySet->set (as a mapping of item->null-node);
  PyFrozenSet->'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply:builtins.frozenset' with value
  [[items…]] (a seq containing one seq); PyComplex->python/complex;
  PyRange->'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply:builtins.range' with [start,stop,step];
  PyObject->'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object:builtins.object' with an empty MappingNode.
  representMapping sorts (key,value) pairs with pySorted/pyCompare and silently keeps the
  original order if a TypeError is raised. flowStyle is always false (default_flow_style=False).
  Compute bestStyle exactly as PyYAML does even though it is then overridden — keep the code
  faithful.
  Anything unrepresentable -> PyError 'RepresenterError'.

/output/lib/yaml/serializer.mjs
  export class Serializer { constructor(emitFn); open(); serialize(node); close() }
  Faithful port of yaml.serializer.Serializer: anchors Map keyed by node object,
  ANCHOR_TEMPLATE 'id%03d' with lastAnchorId starting at 0, anchorNode() depth-first
  (mapping keys before values), serializeNode() emitting AliasEvent for already-serialized
  nodes, and implicit flags computed as described in CONTRACT.md.

/output/lib/yaml/dumper.mjs
  export function dump(data)   // -> the exact string PyYAML's yaml.dump(data) returns
  Wire it up as PyYAML does: create an Emitter writing into a string buffer, emit
  StreamStartEvent, then Serializer.open()+serialize(Representer.represent(data))
  +close(), then StreamEndEvent, and return the buffer.
  Emitter interface (written by another agent):
    import { Emitter } from './emitter.mjs'
    const chunks = []
    const emitter = new Emitter({ write: (s) => chunks.push(s) })
    emitter.emit(event)
  Note: Serializer.open() emits StreamStartEvent and close() emits StreamEndEvent in
  PyYAML; keep the event ORDER as: StreamStart, DocumentStart(explicit=false),
  <node events>, DocumentEnd(explicit=false), StreamEnd.

When done, reply with a terse report: the files you created, the exported names of each, any interface assumption you made that another module must honour, and anything you could not implement. Do not paste the code.

1	# CONTRACT — Node.js port of `/workspace/dataset/test2.py`
2	
3	Original program:
4	
5	```python
6	import yaml, argparse
7	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
8	parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
9	args = parser.parse_args()
10	result = yaml.dump(eval(args.a))
11	print(result)
12	```
13	
14	So: parse `--a`, `eval()` it as a **Python expression**, `yaml.dump()` the result
15	with PyYAML's *unsafe* `Dumper` defaults, `print()` it.
16	
17	Reference binary for differential testing: `/workspace/dataset/test2_executable --a "<expr>"`.
18	**Never** run `python`.
19	
20	## Hard rules
21	
22	* ESM only. `import` / `export`. **No `require`, no `module.exports`.**
23	* Every file ends in `.mjs`; every relative import carries the `.mjs` suffix.
24	* **Zero external packages.** Only `node:*` builtins, and only where truly needed
25	  (`node:process` is fine). Prefer nothing at all.
26	* **`JSON` is forbidden** — never call `JSON.parse` / `JSON.stringify`, never name it.
27	* **`RegExp` is forbidden** — no regex literals (`/.../`), no `new RegExp`, no
28	  `.match` / `.replace` / `.split` / `.test` with a regex argument. All scanning
29	  must be hand-written character loops. (`String.prototype.split` with a *string*
30	  separator, `.replace` with a *string* pattern, `.indexOf`, `.startsWith`,
31	  `.slice`, `.charCodeAt` are all fine.)
32	* No embedded Python, no shelling out.
33	* All code lives under `/output`. Entry point: `/output/test2.mjs`.
34	
35	## Value model
36	
37	Defined and already implemented in `/output/lib/pyvalues.mjs` — read it first.
38	Summary: `int`→`BigInt`, `float`→`Number`, `bool`→`PyBool` singleton, `None`→
39	`PY_NONE`, `str`→JS string, plus `PyBytes`, `PyList`, `PyTuple`, `PySet`,
40	`PyFrozenSet`, `PyDict`, `PyComplex`, `PyRange`, `PyObject`, `PyBuiltin`,
41	`PyFunction`, `PyBoundMethod`. Errors are thrown as `PyError` with `.pyName`
42	(`'TypeError'`, …) and `.pyMessage`.
43	
44	## Module layout
45	
46	```
47	/output/test2.mjs                  entry point
48	/output/lib/pyvalues.mjs           value model            [DONE — do not rewrite]
49	/output/lib/argparse.mjs           argparse subset
50	/output/lib/pyrepr.mjs             Python repr()/str(), float repr, base64
51	/output/lib/python/tokenizer.mjs   Python expression lexer
52	/output/lib/python/parser.mjs      Python expression parser -> AST
53	/output/lib/python/operators.mjs   numeric tower + binary/unary/compare ops
54	/output/lib/python/builtins.mjs    builtin functions + str/list/dict methods
55	/output/lib/python/evaluator.mjs   AST evaluation, `pyEval(source)`
56	/output/lib/yaml/nodes.mjs         ScalarNode / SequenceNode / MappingNode
57	/output/lib/yaml/events.mjs        emitter event objects
58	/output/lib/yaml/resolver.mjs      implicit tag resolution (hand-rolled matchers)
59	/output/lib/yaml/representer.mjs   Python value -> node tree
60	/output/lib/yaml/serializer.mjs    node tree -> event stream (+ anchors)
61	/output/lib/yaml/emitter.mjs       event stream -> text
62	/output/lib/yaml/dumper.mjs        `dump(value)` façade
63	```
64	
65	## Verified reference behaviour (from the binary)
66	
67	### argparse
68	
69	| argv | stdout/stderr | exit |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| `--a 1` / `--a=1` | `1\n...\n\n` | 0 |
72	| (none) | `usage: …\ntest2_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a\n` (stderr) | 2 |
73	| `--a` | `usage: …\ntest2_executable: error: argument --a: expected one argument\n` | 2 |
74	| `--a 1 --a 2` | last wins → `2` | 0 |
75	| `--a -5`, `--a -5.5` | value is `-5` / `-5.5` (matches `^-\d+$` / `^-\d*\.\d+$`) | 0 |
76	| `--a -x`, `--a -2**64` | `argument --a: expected one argument` | 2 |
77	| `--a 1 extra` | `unrecognized arguments: extra` | 2 |
78	| `--a 1 --b 2` | `unrecognized arguments: --b 2` | 2 |
79	| `--A 1`, `-a 1`, `-- --a 1` | `the following arguments are required: --a` | 2 |
80	| `-h` / `--help` | help text below, exit 0 | 0 |
81	
82	Usage line: `usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A`
83	
84	Help text (exit 0, stdout):
85	```
86	usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A
87	
88	options:
89	  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
90	  --a A
91	```
92	Errors go to **stderr** as `usage: …\n` + `test2_executable: error: <msg>\n`, exit 2.
93	Abbreviation matching is on (`--a` is the only long option, so `--a` only).
94	
95	### eval failures
96	
97	Exit code 1, traceback on stderr. Format observed:
98	```
99	Traceback (most recent call last):
100	  File "test2.py", line 8, in <module>
101	  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
102	NameError: name 'foo' is not defined
103	[PYI-989:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test2' due to unhandled exception!
104	```
105	The `PYI-<pid>` number is nondeterministic, so exact bytes cannot be matched;
106	produce the same shape with `process.pid`. For `SyntaxError` the third line is
107	`  File "<string>", line <n>` (no `, in <module>`) followed by the source line
108	and (sometimes) a caret line. Empty input gives `line 0` and an empty source line.
109	
110	### `yaml.dump` settings (PyYAML ≥ 5.1 `Dumper`)
111	
112	`default_flow_style=False`, `default_style=None`, `indent=2`, `width=80`,
113	`allow_unicode=False`, `line_break='\n'`, `explicit_start=False`,
114	`explicit_end=False`, `sort_keys=True`, `encoding=None`, `canonical=False`,
115	`version=None`, `tags=None`.
116	
117	`print(result)` adds one extra `\n` — so a trailing blank line is expected.
118	
119	## PyYAML algorithm to reimplement (verbatim semantics)
120	
121	### Representer dispatch (`yaml.representer.Representer`, exact-type first)
122	
123	| Python type | tag | notes |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| `NoneType` | `tag:yaml.org,2002:null` | value `'null'` |
126	| `str` | `…:str` | value as-is |
127	| `bytes` | `…:binary` | `base64.encodebytes(data).decode('ascii')`, style `'|'` |
128	| `bool` | `…:bool` | `'true'` / `'false'` |
129	| `int` | `…:int` | `str(data)` |
130	| `float` | `…:float` | see below |
131	| `list` | `…:seq` | |
132	| `tuple` | `…:python/tuple` | |
133	| `dict` | `…:map` | |
134	| `set` | `…:set` | as a mapping `{item: None}` |
135	| `frozenset` | `…:python/object/apply:builtins.frozenset` | `[[items…]]` |
136	| `complex` | `…:python/complex` | see below |
137	| `range` | `…:python/object/apply:builtins.range` | `[start, stop, step]` |
138	| `object()` | `…:python/object:builtins.object` with `{}` | |
139	
140	`represent_float`:
141	```python
142	if data != data or (data == 0.0 and data == 1.0):  value = '.nan'
143	elif data == inf:   value = '.inf'
144	elif data == -inf:  value = '-.inf'
145	else:
146	    value = repr(data).lower()
147	    if '.' not in value and 'e' in value:
148	        value = value.replace('e', '.0e', 1)
149	```
150	
151	`represent_complex`:
152	```python
153	if data.imag == 0.0:   s = '%r'    % data.real
154	elif data.real == 0.0: s = '%rj'   % data.imag
155	elif data.imag > 0:    s = '%r+%rj' % (data.real, data.imag)
156	else:                  s = '%r%rj'  % (data.real, data.imag)
157	```
158	
159	`represent_mapping(tag, mapping)`:
160	```python
161	value = []; node = MappingNode(tag, value, flow_style=None)
162	if alias_key is not None: represented_objects[alias_key] = node
163	best_style = True
164	if hasattr(mapping, 'items'):
165	    mapping = list(mapping.items())
166	    try:    mapping = sorted(mapping)
167	    except TypeError: pass
168	for k, v in mapping:
169	    nk = represent_data(k); nv = represent_data(v)
170	    if not (isinstance(nk, ScalarNode) and not nk.style): best_style = False
171	    if not (isinstance(nv, ScalarNode) and not nv.style): best_style = False
172	    value.append((nk, nv))
173	node.flow_style = default_flow_style   # == False
174	```
175	`sorted` compares `(key, value)` tuples and is abandoned wholesale on `TypeError`
176	(use `pySorted` + catch `PyError` with `pyName === 'TypeError'`).
177	`represent_sequence` is the same shape without sorting.
178	
179	`represent_data`:
180	```python
181	alias_key = None if ignore_aliases(data) else id(data)
182	if alias_key is not None and alias_key in represented_objects:
183	    return represented_objects[alias_key]
184	... dispatch on type(data) exactly, then multi-representer object ...
185	```
186	`ignore_aliases(data)` is True for `None`, `()`, and any `str`/`bytes`/`bool`/
187	`int`/`float`. Everything else participates in aliasing **by object identity**.
188	
189	### Serializer
190	
191	```python
192	ANCHOR_TEMPLATE = 'id%03d'
193	def anchor_node(node):
194	    if node in anchors:
195	        if anchors[node] is None: anchors[node] = generate_anchor()  # ++last_anchor_id
196	    else:
197	        anchors[node] = None
198	        for child in children(node): anchor_node(child)   # keys before values
199	def serialize_node(node, parent, index):
200	    alias = anchors[node]
201	    if node in serialized_nodes: emit(AliasEvent(alias)); return
202	    serialized_nodes[node] = True
203	    if Scalar:
204	        detected = resolve(Scalar, value, (True, False))
205	        default  = resolve(Scalar, value, (False, True))   # always :str
206	        implicit = (tag == detected, tag == default)
207	        emit(ScalarEvent(alias, tag, implicit, value, style))
208	    if Sequence: implicit = (tag == ':seq');  emit(SequenceStartEvent(...)) …
209	    if Mapping:  implicit = (tag == ':map');  emit(MappingStartEvent(...)) …
210	```
211	Node identity is **object identity of the node**, so shared representer nodes
212	become anchors/aliases.
213	
214	Event order: `StreamStart, DocumentStart(explicit=False), …nodes…, DocumentEnd(explicit=False), StreamEnd`.
215	
216	### Resolver — implicit scalar tags
217	
218	Registration order matters; matchers are keyed by first character
219	(`''` for the empty string) and tried in registration order, then wildcard (none).
220	
221	1. `bool` — first chars `yYnNtTfFoO` — `^(yes|Yes|YES|no|No|NO|true|True|TRUE|false|False|FALSE|on|On|ON|off|Off|OFF)$`
222	2. `float` — first chars `-+0123456789.` —
223	   `^([-+]?[0-9][0-9_]*\.[0-9_]*([eE][-+][0-9]+)?|\.[0-9_]+([eE][-+][0-9]+)?|[-+]?[0-9][0-9_]*(:[0-5]?[0-9])+\.[0-9_]*|[-+]?\.(inf|Inf|INF)|\.(nan|NaN|NAN))$`
224	   Note the exponent **sign is mandatory** and a `.` is required.
225	3. `int` — first chars `-+0123456789` —
226	   `^([-+]?0b[0-1_]+|[-+]?0[0-7_]+|[-+]?(0|[1-9][0-9_]*)|[-+]?0x[0-9a-fA-F_]+|[-+]?[1-9][0-9_]*(:[0-5]?[0-9])+)$`
227	4. `merge` — first char `<` — `^(<<)$`
228	5. `null` — first chars `~ n N ''` — `^(~|null|Null|NULL|)$`  (empty string matches)
229	6. `timestamp` — first chars `0123456789` —
230	   `^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}|[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{1,2}-[0-9]{1,2}([Tt]|[ \t]+)[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]*)?([ \t]*(Z|[-+][0-9]{1,2}(:[0-9]{2})?))?)$`
231	7. `value` — first char `=` — `^(=)$`
232	8. `yaml` — first chars `!&*` — `^(!|&|\*)$`
233	
234	**Implement these as hand-written character scanners — no RegExp.**
235	`resolve(ScalarNode, value, implicit)` returns the first match, else `:str`.
236	For `SequenceNode`/`MappingNode` it returns `:seq` / `:map`.
237	
238	### Emitter
239	
240	Reimplement `yaml.emitter.Emitter` faithfully: the `expect_*` state machine,
241	`analyze_scalar`, `choose_scalar_style`, `process_tag`, `process_anchor`,
242	`write_indent`, `write_indicator`, `write_plain`, `write_single_quoted`,
243	`write_double_quoted`, `write_literal`, `write_folded`, `determine_block_hints`,
244	`prepare_tag`, `prepare_anchor`, `check_simple_key`, `increase_indent`.
245	
246	`best_indent = 2`, `best_width = 80`, `allow_unicode = False`.
247	
248	Critical details confirmed against the binary:
249	
250	* Root-level scalars: `expect_scalar` does `increase_indent(flow=True)` so the
251	  continuation indent of a folded root scalar is 2.
252	* `write_plain` sets `open_ended = True` when `root_context`; at
253	  `StreamEndEvent` in `expect_document_start`, `open_ended` emits `...` +
254	  `write_indent()`. Hence `yaml.dump(True) == 'true\n...\n'` but
255	  `yaml.dump('yes') == "'yes'\n"`.
256	* Block sequences nested directly in block mappings are **indentless**
257	  (`increase_indent(flow=False, indentless=True)`).
258	* Empty collections fall back to flow style (`[]`, `{}`, `!!set {}`,
259	  `!!python/tuple []`).
260	* `check_simple_key`: total prepared length (anchor + tag + scalar) `< 128`
261	  **and** the scalar is neither empty nor multiline — otherwise `? key` / `: value`.
262	* `ESCAPE_REPLACEMENTS`: `\0 \a \b \t \n \v \f \r \e \" \\ \N(0x85) \_(0xA0)
263	  \L(0x2028) \P(0x2029)`; otherwise `\xHH` / `\uHHHH` / `\UHHHHHHHH`, uppercase hex.
264	* `analyze_scalar` must iterate **code points**, and treat `﻿` as special.
265	  With `allow_unicode=False`, any non-`\n`, non-`\x20..\x7E` character sets
266	  `special_characters = True` → forces double quotes.
267	* `write_double_quoted` fold condition:
268	  `0 < end < len(text)-1 and (ch == ' ' or start >= end) and column + (end-start) > best_width`
269	  → writes `text[start:end] + '\\'`, `write_indent()`, then a leading `'\\'`
270	  if `text[start] == ' '`.
271	* `write_single_quoted` folds a single space when
272	  `start+1 == end and column > best_width and split and start != 0 and end != len(text)`.
273	* `write_plain` folds a single space when `start+1 == end and column > best_width and split`.
274	* `prepare_tag` percent-encodes anything outside
275	  `[0-9A-Za-z] -;/?:@&=+$,_.~*'()[]` (and `!` when the handle is not `!`),
276	  using UTF-8 bytes and `%%%02X`.
277	
278	### Python `repr(float)`
279	
280	Shortest round-trip digits (`Number.prototype.toExponential()` with no
281	argument gives exactly those digits), then:
282	`use_exp = decpt <= -4 || decpt > 16` where `decpt = exponent + 1`.
283	Exponential form: `d[0]` + (`'.' + d[1:]` if more digits) + `e` + sign +
284	exponent zero-padded to ≥ 2 digits. Fixed form adds a trailing `.0` when there
285	would be no fractional digits. Verified: `1e15→1000000000000000.0`,
286	`1e16→1e+16`, `1e-4→0.0001`, `1e-5→1e-05`, `5e-324→5e-324`, `-0.0→-0.0`,
287	`2.0→2.0`, `0.1+0.2→0.30000000000000004`.
288	
289	### `base64.encodebytes`
290	
291	Standard base64, a `\n` after every 76 output characters, and a trailing `\n`
292	(empty input → empty string).
293	
294	## Python expression subset for `eval`
295	
296	Cover generously; tests use data literals but arithmetic and builtins appear:
297	
298	* literals: int (dec/hex/oct/bin, `_` separators), float (`1.`, `.5`, `1e5`),
299	  imaginary (`2j`), strings (`'`, `"`, `'''`, `"""`, prefixes `r b u f rb br
300	  fr rf`, all escapes incl. `\xHH \uHHHH \UHHHHHHHH \N{...}` optional, octal),
301	  bytes, `True`, `False`, `None`, `Ellipsis`/`...`
302	* displays: list, tuple (incl. `()` and `(1,)`), dict (incl. `**`), set,
303	  and list/set/dict/generator comprehensions with multiple `for`/`if`
304	* operators with correct precedence and associativity: `if/else`, `or`, `and`,
305	  `not`, chained comparisons (`< <= > >= == != in "not in" is "is not"`),
306	  `|`, `^`, `&`, `<< >>`, `+ -`, `* / // % @`, unary `+ - ~`, `**`
307	  (right-assoc, binds tighter than unary on its left)
308	* trailers: call (positional, keyword, `*args`, `**kwargs`), `[...]` incl.
309	  slices, `.attr`
310	* `lambda`
311	* builtins: `abs all any bin bool bytes bytearray chr complex dict divmod
312	  enumerate filter float format frozenset hex id int isinstance len list map
313	  max min oct ord pow range repr reversed round set slice sorted str sum tuple
314	  type zip object`
315	* common methods: `str.{upper,lower,strip,lstrip,rstrip,split,rsplit,join,
316	  replace,startswith,endswith,find,index,count,title,capitalize,swapcase,
317	  format,zfill,ljust,rjust,center,encode,isdigit,isalpha,isspace,splitlines}`,
318	  `list.{append,extend,insert,pop,remove,index,count,sort,reverse,copy,clear}`,
319	  `dict.{get,keys,values,items,copy,setdefault,pop,update,fromkeys,clear}`,
320	  `set.{add,discard,remove,union,intersection,difference,copy,update}`,
321	  `bytes.{decode,hex}`, `float.{is_integer}`, `int.{bit_length}`
322	
323	Integer semantics: `int` is arbitrary precision (`BigInt`); `/` always yields
324	`float`; `//` and `%` use **floor** semantics (Python, not JS); `divmod`
325	likewise; `**` with a negative exponent yields `float`; `int ** int` stays exact.
326	`str * int`, `list * int`, `tuple * int` repeat (and `list * n` shares the same
327	element objects, which is what makes anchors appear).

Files created (all ESM, `.mjs`, no RegExp/JSON, zero deps):

**`/output/lib/yaml/nodes.mjs`** — `Node`, `ScalarNode`, `CollectionNode`, `SequenceNode`, `MappingNode`, `TAG`, `DEFAULT_SCALAR_TAG`, `DEFAULT_SEQUENCE_TAG`, `DEFAULT_MAPPING_TAG`. Nodes carry PyYAML's `id` field (`'scalar'`/`'sequence'`/`'mapping'`).

**`/output/lib/yaml/events.mjs`** — `Event`, `NodeEvent`, `CollectionStartEvent`, `CollectionEndEvent`, `StreamStartEvent{encoding}`, `StreamEndEvent`, `DocumentStartEvent{explicit,version,tags}`, `DocumentEndEvent{explicit}`, `AliasEvent{anchor}`, `ScalarEvent{anchor,tag,implicit,value,style}`, `SequenceStartEvent`/`MappingStartEvent{anchor,tag,implicit,flowStyle}`, `SequenceEndEvent`, `MappingEndEvent`; predicates `isStreamStartEvent`, `isStreamEndEvent`, `isDocumentStartEvent`, `isDocumentEndEvent`, `isAliasEvent`, `isScalarEvent`, `isSequenceStartEvent`, `isSequenceEndEvent`, `isMappingStartEvent`, `isMappingEndEvent`, `isCollectionStartEvent`, `isCollectionEndEvent`, `isNodeEvent`. Discriminant is `e.kind` ∈ `StreamStart, StreamEnd, DocumentStart, DocumentEnd, Alias, Scalar, SequenceStart, SequenceEnd, MappingStart, MappingEnd`.

**`/output/lib/yaml/resolver.mjs`** — `resolveScalar`, `resolveScalarDefault`, `resolveSequence`, `resolveMapping`. Hand-written scanners for all 8 implicit resolvers, keyed by first char, registration-ordered; the sexagesimal `(:[0-5]?[0-9])+` groups use an explicit backtracking search. All 54 probe strings from the contract (plus extras: `0:00`→str, `60:00`→int, `1:0.5`→float, `0x_1f`→int, `1__0`→int, `_1`→str, `.e+1`→str) match the binary's quoting behaviour.

**`/output/lib/yaml/representer.mjs`** — `Representer`, plus `pyFloatRepr` (exported). Exact-type dispatch via `typeName`, `representedObjects` keyed by `objectId`, faithful `representScalar/Sequence/Mapping` (alias key captured before recursion, `bestStyle` computed then overridden by `defaultFlowStyle=false`), tuple-wise sort abandoned on `PyError('TypeError')`. Covers None/str/bytes/bool/int/float/list/tuple/dict/set/frozenset/complex/range/slice/`object()`/`python/name` (PyBuiltin→`builtins.X`, PyBoundMethod→`None.X`, PyFunction→`__main__.X`) and Ellipsis→`PyError('ValueError', 'dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required')` (matches the binary). Unknown → `PyError('RepresenterError', ...)`.

**`/output/lib/yaml/serializer.mjs`** — `Serializer(emitFn)` with `open/close/serialize/anchorNode/generateAnchor/serializeNode`, identity-keyed `Map`/`Set`, `id%03d` anchors, implicit flags per contract.

**`/output/lib/yaml/dumper.mjs`** — `dump(data)`. Event order verified: StreamStart, DocumentStart(explicit=false), nodes, DocumentEnd(explicit=false), StreamEnd.

Interface assumptions others must honour:
1. `/output/lib/pyrepr.mjs` must export `base64Encodebytes`. I call it with the raw `Uint8Array` (`PyBytes.bytes`); a `PyBytes`-taking signature is tolerated via a fallback retry, but the export name is mandatory or the whole build fails at link time.
2. `emitter.mjs` must export `Emitter`, constructed as `new Emitter({ write })` with an `emit(event)` method, reading `event.kind`/`instanceof` plus fields `anchor, tag, implicit (2-array), value, style, flowStyle, explicit, version, tags, encoding` (camelCase `flowStyle`, not `flow_style`).
3. Float `repr` is implemented locally as `pyFloatRepr` in representer.mjs rather than imported, to avoid guessing pyrepr's export name — verified byte-identical to the binary on 30 values incl. `1e16`, `5e-324`, `-0.0`, `1e15`, `1.2345678901234568e+16`. If pyrepr exports its own float repr, the two are independent implementations of the same spec.
4. Type objects (`int`, `str`, `type(1)`) must be modelled as `PyBuiltin` with `.name` for `!!python/name:builtins.X` to come out right; a dedicated type class would fall through to `RepresenterError`.

Not implemented: `bytearray` (`!!python/object/apply:builtins.bytearray [text, 'latin-1']`) — the value model has no bytearray type; modules (`python/module:`), and the generic `__reduce_ex__` machinery beyond the builtins listed above. No bugs found in pyvalues.mjs.
